ingredientSections.heading: Seafood Pancake
items: 200g pre-mixed Korean pancake flour, from your local Korean or Asian grocery

methodSections.heading: Dipping Sauce
steps: Mince the garlic and ginger, and very finely chop the green onion.
Measure the soy, vinegar and water into a bowl. Add the sugar and stir until it is dissolved.
Add the remaining ingredients and mix through.

methodSections.heading: Seafood Pancake
steps: In a large bowl mix the pancake flour and water together to create a batter.
Slice the squid into rings, chop the mussels finely and add both to the batter.
Mix together well and let the batter sit in the fridge for an hour.
Remove from the fridge and add the chopped green onions, a drizzle of canola oil and salt to taste (there is already salt mixed in the flour). Mix together well.
Pre-heat the oven to its lowest setting. Add a splash of oil to a large frying pan over a medium low heat. Ladle half of the mixture into the pan and spread evenly.
When the bottom of pancake has browned nicely, flip the pancake and cook the other side.
When cooked, transfer to a plate and place in the oven to keep warm while cooking another pancake with the remaining batter.
Serve on a hot plate with soy sauce, dipping sauce, kimchi, Korean rice and/or lightly pickled vegetables.
